en.title: Leftmost Coordinate Lit by the Most Lamps
en.description:
A lamp (x,r) lights the closed interval [x−r,x+r], with r>0. Return the position lit by the most lamps at once; if several positions tie, take the smallest coordinate.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of x r. The source gives no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, −10⁹≤x≤10⁹, 1≤r≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: the only position shared by all three lamps is 1. Example 2: at most one lamp lights any position, and the leftmost such position is −3. Example 3: the two segments meet at the closed endpoint 1, which is lit by both lamps, so the answer is 1.
hints: For integer coordinates, add 1 at the left end and subtract 1 at the right end plus 1; merge events by coordinate and sweep the coverage count, recording a coordinate only when the maximum coverage is strictly exceeded.
